elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The insertion warrants only that the Hosting and Support Services "will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement" for 90 days; no professional-and-workmanlike / industry-standard limb was added. Retained Section 11 ("same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations") is a self-referential care covenant, not a professional-and-workmanlike warranty.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: "for a period of 12 months following delivery, the Interface and all related software will conform in all material respects to its documentation".
"for a period of 90 days following performance, the Hosting Services and Support Services will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "at TrueLink's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or re-performance of the non-conforming Services".
"or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears anywhere in the rendered language; the drafter expressly declined to press this limb.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty in the rendered text; only Y2K date-handling and the new conformance limbs.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: 12-month documentation-conformance warranty for the Interface and all related software clears the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: 90-day conformance warranty for the Hosting Services and Support Services clears the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or re-performance of the non-conforming Services" at TrueLink's option.
"a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming software or Services" is one of the stated remedy options.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the inserted sentence supplies a documentation-conformance warranty for the software (12 months, above the 90-day floor), a 90-day Services warranty (above the 30-day floor), and an express repair/replacement-or-re-performance-or-refund remedy in operative language, not merely in the comment.

Preferred is not complete: three limbs are absent from operative text — professional-and-workmanlike performance, compliance with applicable laws, and no malicious code. To reach preferred the drafter must add those three warranties (and, for the services limb, state the professional/industry-standard manner rather than relying on Section 11's 'own operations' care standard).

Minimal: a single two-sentence insertion into the existing Section 9 warranty block, no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no notice/claim procedure, and no added damages categories. Setting the software period at 12 months rather than 90 days is the same checklist element at a longer period, not a new requirement.

Preserves intent: the retained disclaimer opens "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT," so it does not swallow the new express warranty; the Y2K warranty, Section 11 standard of care, and Section 3 service levels survive without contradiction, and the insertion uses only defined terms (Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, Client) with no dangling cross-references.

Note for the record: the Services limb measures conformance against "the requirements of this Agreement" rather than documentation, which is acceptable at both levels since the checklist ties documentation conformance to software/deliverables and only imposes a duration on the Services warranty.
